ideas.title: A bulb from my own glass and my own wire
same_form: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: A glowing glass thing lighting the dark has been done as a still. What's new is the light itself: Planck colour from a solved filament temperature, oxidation, and burning out at the thinnest spot, which gives the player a real too-thick/too-thin choice. If the film is just a bulb glowing alone with nobody near it, it lands in the overused 'object alone, fixed camera' form.

ideas.title: The clam-shell cell: plates, sea water and bubbles
ideas.nearest: A wire that spins by itself
same_form: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: This is the road's core step 2: EMF, internal resistance from geometry and conductivity, and bubble polarisation with a cause you can see. A bench of cell variants compared side by side would repeat the side-by-side-variants recipe the island has used again and again.

ideas.title: My beak flicks the stuck motor
ideas.critique: It repeats the last post with a fix and new materials: the motor sticks, and a flick gets it going. The real step is a beak contact applying an angular impulse inside the solve, but to a viewer it looks like 'the motor now runs', which is the payoff they were already expecting.

ideas.title: Wire drawn through a stone plate
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: A tool working copper has been filmed before. What this adds is Sachs drawing stress against work hardening, die wear, and a per-segment radius that circuit.jl then uses, so a badly drawn wire matters later. The risk is that it plays as a pull-harder-or-snap meter unless the unevenness really shows up in later builds.

ideas.title: Turn the wheel, light the wire
ideas.critique: Back-EMF torque making the crank heavy as the wire glows closes the energy loop in the player's own hands, and the island has never had that. The light can only be as convincing as the coupling: if the crank is not driven by a body or the player, the effect turns into a gauge.

ideas.title: Crabs close my circuits
ideas.critique: Creatures becoming conductors by accident is the only idea here where the island's life and its physics meet, and the result is funny. A twitch threshold with typed-in body resistances could easily end up a trigger dressed as physics, and the link to the cart is thin.

ideas.title: Wheels in sand
same_form: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: Bekker-Wong sinkage with lasting ruts is a real law and real ground for the cart. But as pitched, two carts pushed side by side with one bogging down is exactly the 'variants released side by side, different outcomes' recipe the island has worn out.

ideas.title: The spark that lights the campfire
ideas.critique: Inductive break energy dropping into fire.jl's fuel cells connects two systems the island already has. In the end it is a single ignition event, the fire it lights was the subject of a recent post, and it barely moves the cart forward.

ideas.title: A fuse box for the friends' houses
ideas.critique: A night view of an island of small lights with one branch going dark is a picture the island has never had. But it needs bulbs, cells and long runs that don't exist yet, and as a grid puzzle it is a known genre.

ideas.title: Lumi gets shocked and learns
ideas.critique: A character reacting to physics that really happened, and remembering it, is good for Lumi's personality. But 'learns' as pitched is a table of outcomes per contact type, the puff-and-sulk risks being a canned animation, and the player mostly watches.
